As a violinist, I’ve always needed to stay focused during rehearsals and performances, but lately, I can’t keep track of my practice schedule or stick to a routine. Notes go missing, parts of the score blend together. I’ll be halfway into a passage and realize I’ve been thinking about something totally unrelated—like the sound of rain on the roof, or a phrase I heard on the radio yesterday.

People say I’m always moving—tapping my foot, gesturing while I talk. I don’t mean to, but it’s like I can’t sit still. I catch myself talking a lot too, even when others seem overwhelmed. Sometimes, in between movements of a piece, I hear voices calling my name—just faint, like an echo in an empty hall—but no one else hears it. It scares me, but it’s not constant. I don’t know if it’s stress, if I’m just overstimulated, or if something deeper is happening. I just feel... unmoored.
D001-D005_h001.question_a:
I’ve struggled for as long as I can remember—since elementary school, really. I’d lose my sheet music, miss deadlines for rehearsals, and get scolded for not following the conductor’s notes even though I wanted to. Staying focused during practice feels impossible; random thoughts pop up, like ringtones in my head, pulling me away mid-phrase. It’s always been this way—teachers said I was bright but disorganized.

As I got older, it didn’t go away. If anything, it’s harder now. I’m constantly moving—tapping my foot, adjusting my chair, needing to walk around between rehearsals. My colleagues joke that I “never stop talking,” but it’s not funny to me. I’ll start speaking in group chats or meetings without realizing I’ve interrupted someone. I feel driven, like my engine never shuts off.

About six months ago, I started hearing whispers during quiet passages in performances—voices commenting on my playing. That scared me. But here’s the thing: the focus issues, the restlessness, the talking over people—that’s been my whole life. Long before the voices ever showed up. Those symptoms didn’t start because of the hallucinations—they’ve been there since I was a kid.
D001-D005_h001.question_b: I’ve been having a really hard time keeping up with rehearsals lately. I’ve been talking a lot more too—my colleagues have even joked about it—like I can’t stop the words from spilling out, even when I’m not sure what I’m saying. I’m constantly on the move, can’t sit still even after a long day. But the worst part started about six months ago—really intense dreams started bleeding into waking life.
